mainEntity.name: What is an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: An accessory dwelling unit, or ADU, is a self-contained residential living space located on the same parcel of land as a primary single-family home. It includes dedicated sleeping, kitchen, and bathroom facilities. Common configurations include detached backyard cottages, attached additions, above-garage apartments, or converted interior spaces like garages. In multigenerational arrangements, families often refer to them as in-law suites, mother-in-law apartments, or granny flats, though the exact technical classification and structural scope are established during the initial design consultation.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is an independent secondary residential living unit located on the same lot as a primary home, equipped with its own kitchen, bathroom, and living space.
